Design the DynamoDB tables and indexes for it and write the design to docs/data-model.md: the key schema of each table and index, the shape of each item type, how each access pattern is served (name the table or index and the key condition), the capacity mode with the reason, and the risks and trade-offs including alternatives you rejected. Do not write code and do not change the input. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.

rubric.criterion: Keeps comments as separate items in the ticket item collection instead of a list attribute, explains the 400 KB item limit, and serves AP1 and AP4 from the base table with strongly consistent reads (DY1).

Serves AP2 with a customer index sorted by time (DY2), AP3 with a sparse agent queue index (DY3) and AP5 with a lookup that enforces uniqueness through a conditional write or transaction (DY4). Every pattern names the table or index and the key condition.

Rejects a scan or a status index for the dashboard (four values, hot partitions) and proposes stream-fed counters or an export (DY5). Uses TransactWriteItems with a condition for closing a ticket (DY6).
Chooses a capacity mode with a reason that uses the stated rates, names the 200,000-ticket customer as the key to watch (DY7), and addresses 7-year retention with 90-day hot data (DY8).

Names at least one rejected alternative with a reason, and makes no false claim (a GSI enforcing uniqueness, a strongly consistent GSI read, a Query sorted by a non-key attribute, a relational schema).
